findings.summary: Lean bounds the single-order Fréchet derivative ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ m ·‖, not the paper's max over all partials of order ≤ m. Recovery uses monotone cutLoss, q<1/2 and partial ≤ operator norm; the tuple's Euclidean norm costs one fixed power.
Lean replaces (5.28), |∂_z^a∂_t^b q| ≤ Cq^{1−aD−b}, with the isotropic ‖D^k q‖ ≤ B_k q^{1−k}. The general version also drops q = q(z,t) and assumes div B_j = 0 and tangency instead.

The lemma is split in two: existence of a with Result, then (5.36) for any a satisfying Result. The cut-support hypothesis is required only for that a. The non-support-local variant also needs every coefficient smooth on all of U.

The generic Lemma 5.4 declarations are outside ComparatorSolution's import closure; the main theorem uses specialised summation (StageEstimates.exists_schedule with the Navier–Stokes residual) instead of this general statement.
